overview: A one-page Department of State list-of-papers sheet indexes Despatch No. 47 from Dairen, dated December 2, 1940, concerning the proposed marriage of Tatsumi Iwahashi, an American citizen and consular clerk, to a Japanese subject in the Kwantung Leased Territory. The entry notes a request for guidance on making the marriage legally unassailable and recording precisely what occurred, and directs readers to cross-reference 122/2939.

subfiles.about: The sheet indexes a despatch requesting advice on securing a legally unassailable marriage between American consular clerk Tatsumi Iwahashi and a Japanese subject in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: This is a cataloguing sheet rather than the full despatch. It records that Tatsumi Iwahashi, an American citizen employed as a clerk at the consulate in Dairen, intended to marry a Japanese subject on or about December 6, 1940. The referenced despatch sought suggestions for ensuring the marriage’s legal validity and describing precisely what took place; the sheet also refers researchers to file 122/2939.

interest: Although only an index sheet survives here, it identifies a potentially revealing consular case involving nationality, Japanese marriage procedures, and American efforts to ensure the validity of a mixed-nationality marriage in the Japanese-administered Kwantung Leased Territory. Its precise date, despatch number, named participant, and cross-reference to 122/2939 make it especially useful for locating the substantive correspondence elsewhere in the State Department decimal files.
